title: The Hook Garden
text: A field of chains hanging from nothing, swaying, clinking, each ending in an iron hook. Some of the hooks hold the damned, who moan softly as they turn. One, near the middle, holds a key, glinting, turning in the hot wind.

options.label: The quickest snatches the key from its hook, before the chains can catch them.

outcomes.text: The key, to a devil's strongbox, and the box is full.
A hook takes them instead, through the coat and the skin, and it does not want to let go.

options.label: Free the damned on the low hooks, whatever the gardener thinks.

outcomes.text: They thank you, sobbing, and the gardener comes to see who is pruning.

options.label: Go straight through, heads down, and touch nothing.

outcomes.text: Chains brush every shoulder, and every hook turns to follow.
